audience: Short-session browser players who like tension and light puzzles
core_mechanic: Rotate a single lighthouse beam; ships steer toward the beam while rocks stay dark until lit, so the same light that saves one ship exposes another.
title: Lightkeeper: steer ships with one lighthouse beam
why_hot: Tied for first in AI Browser Game Jam 5 on November 16, 2026. Its entire loop is one rotating beam that both reveals and guides, a one-input mechanic with a legible goal.

audience: Puzzle and map players who prefer deduction over reflex
core_mechanic: Take bearings from known stations and triangulate the positions of unseen landmarks; each measurement is a finite resource and the map fills in one fix at a time.
monetization: Free browser listing; no monetization shown
title: Theodolite: map a county by triangulation
why_hot: Listed November 18, 2026 in a 94-game browser drop. A survey game whose whole verb is triangulation, a mechanic a reader can grasp in one line and rarely sees in a web game.

audience: Reflex players who want a 60-second challenge
core_mechanic: The character auto-walks and the only input is a tap that jumps, up to four times in the air; the player must catch ten moving targets without stopping.
title: Stop Walking: one button, four air jumps, ten catches
why_hot: Show HN on November 10, 2026. A one-button 3D rage game with a clear fail state and short levels, the exact shape of a browser session.
